external-reference.meaning: A claim about the world outside the household — an institution's published process, a market convention, a rule of thumb — recorded with its sources and the date it was checked. It is not household data and never carries the verified / calculated / estimated / unknown household trust tags.

items.subject: TD closed-mortgage early-renewal window, rate hold, and renewal contact timing
claims: TD lets a closed mortgage renew early up to 120 days before maturity with no prepayment charge and no fee.
TD's standard rate hold is 120 days, extendable to about 150 days for existing clients. A held rate is a floor, not a commitment.
TD normally makes renewal contact four to five months before maturity and posts the offer letter about a month before maturity. The posted renewal rate is an opening offer, not a fixed price.
A mortgage left unsigned at maturity typically rolls to a short open or posted-rate term, which costs materially more.
Switching lenders needs approval, appraisal and discharge, so the 120-day window is also the point at which a switch becomes practical.

items.subject: Publication status of next-year Canadian payroll statutory tables
claims: As of mid-September 2026, the Canada Revenue Agency had not published the next calendar year's Canada Pension Plan Year's Maximum Pensionable Earnings, additional CPP second-earnings ceiling, Employment Insurance Maximum Insurable Earnings, or federal personal-income-tax indexation amounts. The registered-plans limits table leaves those next-year CPP columns blank.

The latest official payroll-deductions formulas guide in force is the July 2026 T4127 edition. That edition records a Government of Canada intention to reduce the base Canada Pension Plan employee contribution rate from the following January. An intention recorded in a prior-year guide is not itself a next-year contribution-rates table.

British Columbia published a subsequent-year first-bracket personal-income-tax rate after the 2026 mid-year change, and paused indexation of those brackets for several following years. That subsequent-year table is distinct from the mid-year prorated withholding table used for the second half of 2026.

provenance.method: Public web pages read during the 2026-09-16 Atlas research session. No institution login, no household account data, no provider feed.

freshness.review_reason: CRA typically publishes next-year YMPE, EI maxima, and T4127 near calendar year-end. Re-read the official sources before treating next-year statutory tables as known, and at least every 90 days. After review_by, treat the publication-status claim as needing re-checking, not as current.

may_inform.as: explanation of why next-year CPP, EI, and federal indexation are last-published prior-year tables labelled as a planning assumption, and why the British Columbia subsequent-year first-bracket rate is used rather than the mid-year prorated withholding table
